title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from Sweet Wines of the World
objectives: Compare the great sweet wine traditions

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its country.
steps.explanation: Each country has its own great sweet wine.

steps.prompt: What is a trie in Sauternes?
options: A pass through the vineyard to pick botrytised grapes
steps.explanation: Pickers make several tries, taking only the berries that are ready.

steps.prompt: Which wines rely mainly on noble rot?
steps.explanation: Icewine relies on freezing, not botrytis.

steps.prompt: Eszencia often reaches only around 5% alcohol or less.
steps.explanation: Yes. With over 450 g/l of sugar, it ferments very slowly and stays very low in alcohol.

steps.prompt: Château d'Yquem is the only ____ Cru Supérieur in the 1855 classification.
steps.explanation: Yquem holds the unique rank of Premier Cru Supérieur.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Botrytis concentrates sugar and adds honeyed aromas
Sauternes, Tokaji and German TBA are botrytis wines
Ice wine and passito use frost and drying
High acidity keeps all great sweet wines fresh
